GROWTH FOUNDATION — MODULE 5

Communicate Clearly. Connect Intentionally. Work Effectively. Create Results.

---

MODULE OVERVIEW

Every person who wants to grow will eventually need to work with people.

You may have knowledge, a degree, a business idea, technical skills, money, a product, an office, a job or a vision. But if you cannot communicate your value, understand people, work with people, manage disagreements, build relationships and influence responsibly, your capability may remain limited.

Communication is therefore not merely a social skill.

It is a personal, professional, economic, leadership and institutional capability.

You use communication to:

- get employed

- sell

- negotiate

- lead

- teach

- manage

- build relationships

- attract customers

- work in teams

- solve problems

- present ideas

- manage conflict

- build partnerships

- serve citizens

- manage organizations

- create opportunities

- influence decisions

- coordinate people toward results

SGG PRINCIPLE

«Communication is the bridge between what you know and the value other people can understand, trust and act upon.»

lessons.title: 5.5 WHAT COMMUNICATION REALLY MEANS
Content: Communication is the process of creating and exchanging meaning between people.
It involves more than sending information.
SENDER → MESSAGE → CHANNEL → RECEIVER → INTERPRETATION → RESPONSE → FEEDBACK
The employee may interpret “soon” as tomorrow.
The manager may mean within one hour.
The message was sent, but communication was not sufficiently clear.
«“Please send the completed report by 3:00 p.m. today.”»
«Communication is not successful simply because you spoke. It is successful when the intended meaning is understood well enough for the appropriate next action to occur.»

blocks.content:
Communication is the process of creating and exchanging meaning between people.

It involves more than sending information.

A simple communication process is:

SENDER → MESSAGE → CHANNEL → RECEIVER → INTERPRETATION → RESPONSE → FEEDBACK

For example:

A manager says:

«“I need the report soon.”»

The employee may interpret “soon” as tomorrow.

The manager may mean within one hour.

The message was sent, but communication was not sufficiently clear.

Better:

«“Please send the completed report by 3:00 p.m. today.”»

LESSON

«Communication is not successful simply because you spoke. It is successful when the intended meaning is understood well enough for the appropriate next action to occur.»

---

lessons.title: 5.6 THE FIVE QUESTIONS BEFORE COMMUNICATING
Content: Before communicating an important message, ask:
What exactly am I trying to communicate?
What is the best channel and approach?
What should happen after the communication?

blocks.content:
Before communicating an important message, ask:

1. WHAT?

What exactly am I trying to communicate?

2. WHY?

Why does this communication matter?

3. WHO?

Who am I communicating with?

4. HOW?

What is the best channel and approach?

5. WHAT NEXT?

What should happen after the communication?

This prevents careless communication.

lessons.title: 5.7 THE SGG COMMUNICATION OPERATING SYSTEM
Content: Students should learn this simple system:
THINK → STRUCTURE → COMMUNICATE → LISTEN → CLARIFY → RESPOND → ACT → REVIEW
This framework can be used in:

blocks.content:
Students should learn this simple system:

THINK → STRUCTURE → COMMUNICATE → LISTEN → CLARIFY → RESPOND → ACT → REVIEW

THINK

Understand your objective.

STRUCTURE

Organize your thoughts.

COMMUNICATE

Deliver the message.

LISTEN

Observe the response.

CLARIFY

Correct misunderstanding.

RESPOND

Address what matters.

ACT

Move toward the desired outcome.

REVIEW

Learn from the interaction.

This framework can be used in:

- business

- career

- government

- family

- education

- leadership

- customer service

- sales

- teamwork.

PART ONE — VERBAL COMMUNICATION

lessons.title: 5.8 VERBAL COMMUNICATION
Content: Verbal communication is communication through spoken language.

lessons.title: 5.9 THE 7Cs OF EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION
Content: A useful SGG framework is the 7Cs.
Make your message easy to understand.
Consider the person, context and circumstances.
«“Please review the customer's complaint and send me your proposed solution by 2:00 p.m.”»

blocks.content:
A useful SGG framework is the 7Cs.

1. CLEAR

Make your message easy to understand.

2. CONCISE

Remove unnecessary words.

3. COMPLETE

Provide the information required.

4. CORRECT

Use accurate information.

5. CONCRETE

Use specific language.

6. COHERENT

Make your ideas logically connected.

7. CONSIDERATE

Consider the person, context and circumstances.

Example

Weak:

«“Please handle the matter quickly.”»

Better:

«“Please review the customer's complaint and send me your proposed solution by 2:00 p.m.”»

The second message is:

- clearer;

- more specific;

- actionable;

- easier to measure.

---

lessons.title: 5.10 HOW TO SPEAK CLEARLY
Content: What is the main thing I need to say?

«“We need to change our customer follow-up process because several enquiries are not being answered promptly. I recommend that every new enquiry be acknowledged within two hours and followed up within 24 hours.”»

blocks.content:
Use this sequence:

POINT

What is the main thing I need to say?

REASON

Why does it matter?

DETAIL

What information is necessary?

ACTION

What needs to happen next?

For example:

«“We need to change our customer follow-up process because several enquiries are not being answered promptly. I recommend that every new enquiry be acknowledged within two hours and followed up within 24 hours.”»

The listener understands:

- the issue;

- the reason;

- the solution;

- the expected action.

---

lessons.title: 5.11 SPEAKING WITH CONFIDENCE
Content: - being honest about what you do not know;
«Confidence is not the absence of uncertainty. It is the ability to communicate responsibly despite uncertainty.»

lessons.title: 5.12 LISTENING
Content: Many people are waiting for their turn to speak rather than listening to understand.
Listening is a critical professional capability.

lessons.title: 5.13 HEARING VS LISTENING
Content: Making a deliberate effort to understand meaning.
A person can hear every word and still fail to listen.

blocks.content:
HEARING

Receiving sound.

LISTENING

Making a deliberate effort to understand meaning.

A person can hear every word and still fail to listen.

---

lessons.title: 5.14 ACTIVE LISTENING
Content: Active listening means giving intentional attention to the speaker and demonstrating that you are trying to understand.
Allow the person to complete their thought.
«“If I understand you correctly, your main concern is the delivery timeline. Is that right?”»
Respond to what was actually communicated.

blocks.content:
Active listening means giving intentional attention to the speaker and demonstrating that you are trying to understand.

It includes:

1. Attention

Remove unnecessary distractions.

2. Patience

Allow the person to complete their thought.

3. Questions

Ask questions to understand.

4. Clarification

Resolve ambiguity.

5. Paraphrasing

Restate the important point.

Example:

«“If I understand you correctly, your main concern is the delivery timeline. Is that right?”»

6. Appropriate response

Respond to what was actually communicated.

---

lessons.title: 5.15 THE SGG LAST MODEL
Content: This model should become a practical habit.

blocks.content:
L — LISTEN

Pay attention.

A — ASK

Ask clarifying questions.

S — SUMMARIZE

Explain what you understood.

T — TAKE ACTION

Respond appropriately.

This model should become a practical habit.

PART THREE — WRITTEN COMMUNICATION

lessons.title: 5.16 WRITTEN COMMUNICATION
Content: Your writing often represents you when you are not physically present.
«Your writing is part of your professional identity.»

lessons.title: 5.17 THE PROFESSIONAL WRITING STANDARD
Content: Do not use complicated language merely to sound intelligent.
The goal is understanding, not vocabulary competition.

lessons.title: 5.18 PROFESSIONAL EMAIL STRUCTURE
Content: What does the recipient need to know?

blocks.content:
A professional email normally follows:

State the purpose.

GREETING

Address the recipient appropriately.

PURPOSE

Why are you writing?

CONTEXT

What does the recipient need to know?

REQUEST/ACTION

What needs to happen?

DEADLINE

When is it required?

CLOSING

End professionally.

lessons.title: 5.19 PROFESSIONAL DIGITAL COMMUNICATION
Content: The fact that communication is digital does not remove professionalism.

lessons.title: 5.20 PRESENTATION SKILLS
Content: A presentation is a structured way of helping an audience understand:
A presentation is not simply reading slides.

Content: Capture attention and establish the purpose.
Why should the audience take this seriously?

blocks.content:
OPENING

Capture attention and establish the purpose.

CONTEXT

Explain the situation.

PROBLEM

What needs attention?

MAIN POINTS

Explain the important information.

SOLUTION

What should be done?

EVIDENCE

Why should the audience take this seriously?

ACTION

What should happen next?

---

For short presentations:

1

One central message.

3

1

Yourself → One person → Small group → Team → Larger audience

Content: What should they understand or do next?

blocks.content:
PURPOSE

Content: Nervousness is not automatically evidence of inability.
- use notes rather than memorizing every sentence.
The objective is not to impress the audience.
The objective is to deliver value to the audience.

lessons.title: 5.26 WHAT IS NEGOTIATION?
Content: Negotiation is a process in which people communicate about differing interests and seek an agreement.

lessons.title: 5.27 NEGOTIATION PREPARATION
Content: What am I not prepared to accept?
What might the other party need?
What would a workable agreement look like?

blocks.content:
Before negotiating, identify:

MY OBJECTIVE

What do I want?

MY PRIORITIES

What matters most?

MY LIMITS

What am I not prepared to accept?

THEIR INTERESTS

What might the other party need?

MY VALUE

What can I offer?

ALTERNATIVES

What other options exist?

POSSIBLE AGREEMENT

What would a workable agreement look like?

---

lessons.title: 5.28 POSITION VS INTEREST
Content: A position is what someone says they want.
An interest is why they want it.
«“The project must be completed by Friday.”»
«“The client is presenting the project on Monday.”»
Understanding the interest can create more options.

blocks.content:
A position is what someone says they want.

An interest is why they want it.

Example:

Position:

«“The project must be completed by Friday.”»

Possible interest:

«“The client is presenting the project on Monday.”»

Understanding the interest can create more options.

The process becomes:

POSITION → INTEREST → OPTIONS → AGREEMENT

---

lessons.title: 5.29 NEGOTIATION ETHICS
Content: - hide material facts where disclosure is required;
The objective is to create a workable agreement while protecting legitimate interests.

lessons.title: 5.31 SEPARATE PEOPLE FROM PROBLEMS
Content: «“The agreed deadline was Tuesday, and the report was not submitted. Let's understand what happened and determine how to prevent another delay.”»

blocks.content:
Instead of:

«“You are careless.”»

Use:

«“The agreed deadline was Tuesday, and the report was not submitted. Let's understand what happened and determine how to prevent another delay.”»

Address:

Behaviour → Impact → Solution

rather than attacking:

Identity → Character → Dignity

Content: How does the other person understand it?
What effect did the issue create?

blocks.content:
PAUSE

FACT

PERSPECTIVE

IMPACT

PART NINE — PROFESSIONAL ETIQUETTE

lessons.title: 5.37 WHAT IS PROFESSIONAL ETIQUETTE?
Content: Professional etiquette is the collection of behaviours that help people work together respectfully and effectively.

lessons.title: 5.38 PROFESSIONAL ETIQUETTE RULES
Content: Do what you agreed to do.
People may have different backgrounds and working styles.

blocks.content:
Respect people.

Regardless of status.

Respect time.

Be punctual and prepared.

Respect commitments.

Do what you agreed to do.

Respect information.

Handle confidential information responsibly.

Respect differences.

People may have different backgrounds and working styles.

Respect professional boundaries.

Friendliness does not remove professionalism.

---

BEFORE

- Know the purpose.

- Review relevant information.

- Prepare questions.

- Arrive on time.

- Test technology if necessary.

DURING

- Listen.

- Contribute.

- Avoid unnecessary interruption.

- Stay relevant.

- Record decisions.

AFTER

- Complete assigned actions.

- Communicate delays.

- Follow up.

- Review unresolved issues.

PART TEN — TEAMWORK

lessons.title: 5.40 TEAMWORK

What are we trying to achieve?
How will members support one another?

PART ELEVEN — EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE

lessons.title: 5.43 WHAT IS EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE?
Content: Emotional intelligence involves recognizing, understanding and appropriately managing emotions in yourself and in interactions with others.
It means developing the ability to recognize emotional responses and choose appropriate behaviour.

lessons.title: 5.44 FOUR PRACTICAL AREAS
Content: What might the other person be experiencing?
How can we work effectively together?

blocks.content:
1. SELF-AWARENESS

What am I feeling?

What triggered it?

2. SELF-MANAGEMENT

How should I respond?

3. SOCIAL AWARENESS

What might the other person be experiencing?

4. RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT

How can we work effectively together?

lessons.title: 5.45 THE EMOTIONAL PAUSE
Content: Determine the response that aligns with your values and objective.
This can be especially useful during:

blocks.content:
When emotionally triggered:

STOP

Do not immediately react.

NAME

Identify the emotion.

UNDERSTAND

Identify the trigger.

CHOOSE

Determine the response that aligns with your values and objective.

ACT

Respond intentionally.

This can be especially useful during:

- criticism;

- conflict;

- customer complaints;

- negotiation;

- workplace pressure;

- difficult conversations.

lessons.title: 5.52 THE FOUR-TIER APPLICATION
Content: Who am I and how do I grow?
The learner can communicate professionally and work effectively with people in everyday personal and professional situations.
How do I create value and produce results?
The learner can use communication to generate opportunities, serve customers, execute projects and create measurable results.
How do I lead, build and scale?
The learner can use communication to align people, manage teams, resolve organizational problems and drive execution.
How do I create lasting institutional impact?
The learner can communicate at institutional and strategic levels across complex stakeholder environments.

lessons.title: 5.71 COMMON COMMUNICATION FAILURES TO ELIMINATE
Content: 11. Attacking people instead of addressing problems.
16. Treating digital communication as informal by default.

blocks.content:
Students should watch for:

1. Speaking without thinking.

2. Listening only to reply.

3. Constant interruption.

4. Complicated language.

5. Making assumptions.

6. Communicating while angry.

7. Sending unclear messages.

8. Failing to follow up.

9. Making promises without capacity.

10. Avoiding difficult conversations.

11. Attacking people instead of addressing problems.

12. Confusing confidence with loudness.

13. Ignoring cultural differences.

14. Sharing confidential information carelessly.

15. Using AI without verification.

16. Treating digital communication as informal by default.

17. Failing to document important agreements.

18. Refusing constructive feedback.

19. Communicating without considering the audience.

20. Forgetting that behaviour also communicates.

blocks.content:

2. Listen before responding.

3. Ask before assuming.

4. Clarify before concluding.

5. Write clearly.

6. Keep commitments.

7. Follow up.

8. Give constructive feedback.

9. Receive correction professionally.

Content: At School of Growth Global, people skills should not be taught as manipulation techniques.

At School of Growth Global, people skills should not be taught as manipulation techniques.

The goal is:

Influence without manipulation.

Confidence without arrogance.

Assertiveness without disrespect.

Leadership without humiliation.

Content: You will meet people throughout your life.

Your ability to communicate will influence how effectively you navigate these relationships.
Therefore, do not become merely a person who knows how to speak.

You will meet people throughout your life.

Some will teach you.

Think clearly.

Listen deeply.

Understand people.

Present ideas.

Negotiate responsibly.

Manage conflict.

Build relationships.

Work with teams.

Manage emotions.

Create trust.

Create value.

Create results.
